SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaints: 2-month history of escalating anxiety related to new, stressful job; daily dread of leaving house; palpitations on waking; poor sleep (est. 3–4 hrs/night); low energy and anhedonia. No prior similar episodes.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began ≈2 months ago, coinciding with starting new retail-sector head-office job. Symptoms worsening.
- Associated features:
  • Palpitations: irregular, rapid heartbeat lasting minutes (up to ≈10 min), mainly on mornings when anticipating work; no chest pain except awareness of fast heartbeat.  
  • Sleep: difficulty initiating sleep (lies awake “for hours”), early awakening with racing heart.  
  • Mood: persistent low mood, loss of enjoyment; denies suicidal ideation or past attempts.  
  • Avoidance: declining social/physical activities; occasional avoidance of friends; continues to attend work daily.  
  • Appetite: largely unchanged; increased chocolate intake.  
  • No history of panic attacks to date.
- Past medical history: not discussed.
- Previous surgeries: not discussed.
- Medications: none reported.
- Social history: Lives with parents; employed full-time in fashion-retail head office. Alcohol—binge pattern: exceeds recommended limits on Fri/Sat; occasional weekday wine. Smoking—occasional; denies illicit drug use. Supportive family.
- Allergies: not discussed.

Objective:
- No vital signs or physical examination recorded during tele-consultation.
- Mental state (observed via video): appeared distressed when describing anxiety; speech coherent; no suicidal ideation; insight preserved.
- Investigations: Basic blood tests (type unspecified) planned to assess for reversible causes of palpitations/anxiety.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Work-related anxiety / probable Generalized Anxiety Disorder
   - Assessment: Likely Generalized Anxiety Disorder precipitated by new job stress.
   - Differential diagnosis: Adjustment disorder, emerging depressive episode.
   - Investigations planned: Baseline blood tests (e.g., FBC, TSH, electrolytes) – patient to arrange via support line.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Provide NHS self-referral link for talking therapy (IAPT/Cognitive Behavioral Therapy).  
     • Supply online anxiety-management resources.  
     • Advise patient to recontact GP if symptoms worsen or interfere with work/ADLs.  
   - Follow-up: GP appointment 1 week after blood tests to review results and symptom progress.

2. Palpitations
   - Assessment: Palpitations likely secondary to anxiety.
   - Differential diagnosis: Arrhythmia, thyrotoxicosis, anemia (to be ruled out with labs).
   - Investigations planned: Same baseline blood tests as above; consider ECG if symptoms persist or abnormal labs/clinical concern.
   - Treatment planned: Address underlying anxiety; safety-net advice to seek urgent care if chest pain, syncope, or prolonged palpitations occur.

3. Insomnia / Sleep disturbance
   - Assessment: Insomnia secondary to anxiety.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Provide written sleep-hygiene advice.  
     • Reinforce CBT resources targeting insomnia.  
     • Monitor response; consider pharmacologic options if conservative measures fail (none initiated today).

Quality checks:
• Missing but clinically expected: Detailed past medical history, current medication list, drug and environmental allergies, objective vitals, cardiovascular/thyroid examination.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear with minimal background noise; no major inaudible sections.
